postgres: PostgreSQL 17.11 on x86_64-pc-linux-musl, compiled by gcc (Alpine 15.2.0) 15.2.0, 64-bit

proofs.name: Blueprint scenarios run against the real engine
proofs.claim: Every scenario each blueprint declares, executed by the runtime that would run it in production.

proofs.name: Authorization is enforced by the runtime, not by the caller
proofs.claim: Section 6.1 IAM-03: every authorization check is enforced server-side. Section 12.1: deny by default.
proofs.detail: Refused: a manager from another tenant ("principal belongs to a different tenant"), an operator without the capability ("no role held (it_operator) has the "approve" capability"), a manager the request does not name ("actor is not named as an approver on this request"), and a respondent ("a respondent may not approve"). Payroll fields came back redacted to the hiring manager while the job title did not. An edit outside the role's editable fields was refused. The named approver was allowed. 5 refusals are on the audit record.

proofs.name: A form can be filled in, saved, submitted, and amended when asked
proofs.claim: Section 21 P0: value cannot exist without trustworthy intake. Section 20.1 steps 4 and 6.
proofs.detail: The published form served no classifications, roles or workflow. A hidden section appeared only once its condition was met. A half-finished draft reopened with its answers and created 0 records, because a draft is not a case. An incomplete submission was refused with 14 named fields; a complete one started a process and returned a resume link, and the draft could not be used again. Asked for changes ("Your phone number has a digit missing."), the respondent updated their phone number and was refused their bank account ("bank_account") — which the blueprint declares and nothing until now enforced.

proofs.name: A resume link opens one record and no others
proofs.claim: Section 12.3: broken object authorization in public resume and file links.
proofs.detail: The holder read their own record and was refused somebody else's ("resume token is for a different record"). A respondent with no token was refused even their own ("respondent has no resume token for any record"), and approving was refused ("a respondent may not approve"). Revoking the link made it resolve to nothing. Before this, "a respondent may view" meant any record in the tenant.

proofs.name: A worker fires deadlines with nobody watching
proofs.claim: Section 10.1: queue-backed workers. A deadline that needs an operator to open a page is not a deadline.
proofs.detail: Forty-nine hours passed with no request of any kind. The loop settled in 3 round(s), sent 1 reminder and left 0 due timers unfired.

proofs.name: Retention deletes, only for an administrator, and says what it removed
proofs.claim: Sections 9.2 and 12.1: configurable retention and deletion jobs, against an append-only history.
proofs.detail: An operator was refused ("neither the roles held (it_operator) nor workspace role "operator" grant "administer""). The preview reported 1 instance and 1 events and deleted nothing. The real run removed 1 instance and 1 events, leaving a retention_run row naming what went. The record still inside its retention period survived, and deleting its history outside the procedure is still refused.

proofs.name: Idempotent email under replay
proofs.claim: Section 6.5: a stable action key prevents duplicate emails, documents, webhooks, or charges.
proofs.detail: 1 email(s) after first delivery, 1 after two full replays. The outbox row was delivered 3 times; the action ran 3 time(s) and every replay short-circuited on the idempotency key.

proofs.name: Concurrent workers never double-process
proofs.claim: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED gives each outbox row to exactly one worker, with no lock waits between them.
proofs.detail: 8 workers claimed 40 rows across 4 distinct worker ids; 40 emails for 40 instances (1 each), 0 duplicated effects.

proofs.name: A dead worker loses nothing and duplicates nothing
proofs.claim: A claimed row is invisible for its visibility timeout, then returns to the queue for someone else.
proofs.detail: Another worker saw 0 rows at +5s and 1 at +45s. The record reached "manager_review" with 1 email sent, not 2.

proofs.name: Timers fire once, on time, and are cancelled on exit
proofs.claim: Section 6.5: relative deadlines and reminders, stored canonically in UTC.
proofs.detail: Nothing at +47h, 1 firing at +49h, 0 on a second sweep at the same instant. 1 reminder sent; 1 pending timer(s) cancelled when the record moved on.

proofs.name: A double submission makes one case
proofs.claim: Section 4.2: duplicates are handled without losing the original audit trail.
proofs.detail: 1 instance from 2 concurrent submissions, 1 receipt sent. The second attempt is still on the record as "duplicate_submission_ignored".

proofs.name: A published version cannot be edited, and a live record keeps the version it started under
proofs.claim: Section 9.2: published versions are immutable; every instance records the version that governs it.
proofs.detail: Editing v1 was refused by the database, not by convention. Editing its event history was refused too. v2 is live, and the in-flight record still runs under v1.

proofs.name: Submission and workflow start are far inside the section 10.4 budget
proofs.claim: Beta targets: acknowledgment p95 under 1.5s, workflow start p95 under 30s.
proofs.detail: Over 100 submissions: acknowledgment p95 15.6ms (budget 1500ms), first action p95 33.0ms (budget 30000ms). Database round trips only, local container.
